workload.name: stock xv6-public forktest, 4 MiB, Bochs BIOS
workload.commandBase: XV6_LEAN=1 XV6_FIRMWARE=bochs XV6_STEPS=40000000 XV6_STOP_ON_EXPECT=1 XV6_COMMAND=$'forktest\r' XV6_EXPECT_SERIAL=$'fork test OK\n$ ' node scripts/probe-xv6-stock.mjs
workload.normalization: Remove nativeByte, nativeStats and sharedRam fields; replace rom, image and slaveImage absolute paths with <media>; retain all other report fields in original JSON order.

implementation.change: Add 32-bit register-immediate MOV and CMP (including sign-extended 83 /7) to the opt-in decoder and WASM IR. Copy CPU registers, EIP, flags and cycle state directly between the JavaScript CPU and shared WASM state to avoid per-call arrays.

validation: node --test test/i80386*.test.mjs: 353 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed. Full xv6 ordinary and native guest reports match after opt-in metadata and absolute media path normalization.
conclusion: Direct CPU state transfer saves measurable host work, while the average native call still retires fewer than 2.5 instructions. This path is slower than ordinary JavaScript stepping and remains opt-in.
